what: Coca-Cola Consolidated is the largest Coca-Cola bottler in the United States. It does not own the brands: it buys concentrate from The Coca-Cola Company, bottles it, and delivers to shops across the Southeast and Midwest.
customers: Supermarkets, convenience stores, restaurants and vending operators in about 14 states.
money: Coca-Cola, Sprite, Fanta and Diet Coke
Dasani, Powerade, Gold Peak and Monster distribution
moat: An exclusive territory. Within its franchise area no other bottler may sell Coca-Cola products, which makes the route network and shelf relationships a protected business.
risks: The brand owner sets concentrate prices, and the bottler has to absorb or pass them on
Volumes of sugary carbonated drinks decline slowly year after year
$2.9B of debt against $282M of cash, and no analyst coverage to speak of
opportunities: Revenue grew from $5.6B to $7.2B in four years, mostly on price rather than volume
A 7.9% net margin, high for a bottler, which shows pricing is sticking
Growth in sports drinks, water and energy distribution offsets the decline in soda
watch: Price per case against volume, which shows whether increases are costing sales.
